newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel minister says investments linked to peace.
newsitem.headline: Israel minister says investments linked to peace.

text.p: Israel's Finance Minister Dan Meridor said on Thursday peace and stability were necessary to attract foreign investment to Israel and other parts of the Middle East.

In an interview with Israel Radio from Washington, Meridor said: "The smaller the risk and the greater the stability (in the area) the higher the investments. The peace process is absolutely linked to this."

"It is true that Israeli growth started well before the Oslo (peace) process, but there is no doubt that if (investors) see that the region is stabilising there will be more investments. If they see it is not stabilising, there will be less investments."

Meridor, in Washington for the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund, said foreign investors look at the long term. Thus it was important for them to believe the peace process would go on.
U.S. President Bill Clinton convened a two-day summit in an attempt to defuse tensions between Israelis and Palestinians following bloody clashes last week that killed 73 people.

The summit achieved no concrete results but the two sides agreed to talks starting on Sunday under U.S. mediation. Meridor backed the outcome of the summit and said Israel and the Palestinians needed to continue negotiations.
"The economic issue could be an instrument to stabilise the situation, to create with them (Palestinians) an interest not to go back to terror," he added.
